newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends flat vs mark, rises on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends flat vs mark, rises on dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 994.50-995.20 per mark, in a narrower spread than the opening 994-995.50, as interbank trade thinned to a trickle in the afternoon, dealers said.

* Foreign currency supply topped demand in the morning amid brisk trade as a deadline expired for banks to deposit July's minimum required reserves with the central bank and for companies to make advance corporate tax payments for August.
* The lev rose to 1,825-1,829 per dollar in late trade from the morning's 1,833-1,835, tracking weakening dollar/mark on global markets.

* The dollar was quoted at 1,813-1,818 levs around 1630 local time (1300 GMT) in line with accelerating mark gains abroad. But no deals were reported at those levels as most local banks had left the market by that time.

* The lev was pegged at 1,000 per mark as an anchor under a currency board system, a form of an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate mechanism designed to curb inflation, restore confidence in the lev and stabilise the economy.
* Under the system introduced on July 1 the central bank pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor currency at 995 levs bid and 1,000 ask. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
